title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook Comprehensive
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines Redwood Inference’s on-call and incident response standards: severity definitions, paging and escalation policies, runbook templates, postmortem process, on-call rotations, game-day guidance, and standardized status page / customer communications. It is intended for engineers, on-call responders, SRE, customer success, and product stakeholders.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: provide a single, company-wide source of truth for responding to production incidents that impact customer experience, security, or availability.
- Scope: covers Redwood-hosted inference services, Dedicated control plane, Private deployment support path, and customer-facing status and communications. Internal-only operational tactics are included here; sensitive customer-specific content lives in customer-specific runbooks (restricted).

Definitions and incident severities:
- Sev1 (Critical): customer-visible outage or severe degradation affecting >20% of requests or core control plane unavailable. Requires immediate paging and 24x7 response. Target MTTR: under 2 hours.
- Sev2 (High): significant degradation or partial outage affecting a subset of customers or non-critical control plane capability. Target MTTR: under 8 hours.
- Sev3 (Medium): degraded performance or intermittent errors with limited customer impact. Target MTTR: under 3 business days.
- Sev4 (Low): minor issues, documentation requests, or non-urgent maintenance items. Handled in normal business hours.

SLOs and alerting thresholds (examples):
- Redwood API availability (monthly): 99.95% (objective).
- Request p95 latency (hosted text generation): < 300 ms.
- Error rate (5xx) by model route: < 0.5% sustained.
- Alerting rules should map to SLOs: e.g., error-rate spike > 1% sustained for 5m -> Sev2; regional availability drop > 2% -> Sev1.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Primary on-call (Owner): first responder, triage, mitigation, and initial customer comms.
- Secondary on-call (Backup): assists and takes over if primary is unavailable.
- On-call manager: ensures handoffs, escalations, and post-incident reviews are completed.
- Incident commander (IC): appointed for Sev1/Sev2 to coordinate cross-team work and communications.
- SRE/infra escalation: for capacity, network, and infra incidents.
- Customer Success / Support: owns external customer comms and status updates with input from IC.

Paging & escalation policy:
1) Pager systems: PagerDuty is the source of truth for alerts and routing. All responders must keep on-call schedule up to date and maintain valid contact methods.
2) First page: Primary on-call (5m response expectation during on-call shift).
3) If no ack in 5 minutes: page secondary.
4) After 15 minutes with no resolution or if severity rises: escalate to the on-call manager and designate an IC.
5) If issue impacts production broadly (Sev1): immediately open incident channel (Slack #incident-<id>), notify exec on-call and Customer Success.

Incident response runbook structure (standard):
- Title: short descriptive name.
- Symptoms: what is observed (metrics, dashboards, logs).
- Impact & scope: who/what is affected.
- Ownership: primary, secondary, and escalation contacts.
- Immediate mitigation steps: actionable commands, toggles, quick rollbacks.
- Investigation steps: logs, traces, commands to collect artifacts.
- Recovery steps: how to restore service, route traffic, or execute rollback.
- Post-incident actions: postmortem, corrective work, follow-ups.
- Links: related dashboards, runbooks, playbooks, and runbook pages.

Example runbook: "Model-serving high 5xx rate / OOM on GPU nodes"
- Symptoms:
  - Increased 5xx errors observed on redwood-api:route=/v1/generate from 2026-01-11 10:04 UTC.
  - Node GPU memory pressure alerts firing.
  - Customer reports timeouts and increased latency.
- Immediate mitigation:
  1. Open incident channel: #incident-<timestamp>-model-oom and invite SRE, runtime, infra, and CS.
  2. Fail over traffic to fallback model variant: update router rule in control plane (api call):

   curl -X POST https://platform-api.redwood.internal/v1/routes/<route>/failover -H 'Authorization: Bearer $RD_API_TOKEN' -d '{"fallback_model":"redwood/gptx-small-quant-v2"}'

  3. Mark affected nodes in fleet as unschedulable:

   kubectl cordon <node-name> -n inference-fleet
   kubectl drain <node-name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n inference-fleet

  4. If immediate memory pressure: restart runtime process on node: systemctl restart inference-runtime || sudo docker restart inference-runtime

- Investigation:
  - Collect logs: kubectl logs -n inference-fleet --since=30m <pod>
  - Check GPU memory metrics in Grafana dashboard: GPU Memory Utilization by node.
  - Review recent model rollout history and quantization changes.

- Recovery:
  - Scale up pool (if autoscale insufficient): terraform apply -var 'pool_size+=2' -target=module.inference_pool (follow infra runbook) OR request manual node addition via infra runbook.
  - Once stable, gradually route traffic back using canary policy: 10% -> 30% -> 100% over 15-minute intervals while monitoring 5xx and latency.

- Post-incident actions:
  - Owner to file postmortem within 72 hours.
  - Create follow-up tickets for root cause fixes and automation (e.g., better OOM handling, autoscale tuning).

On-call rotations and handoffs:
- Rotation cadence: weekly rotation for primary on-call (Mon 08:00 UTC -> next Mon 08:00 UTC). Secondary rotates weekly and is offset by 3 days where feasible.
- Shift length: 7 days. Exception for planned absences must be updated in PagerDuty and Slack.
- Handoffs: mandatory written handoff note in #oncall-handoffs channel and update on-call calendar. The outgoing on-call must summarize ongoing incidents, mitigation state, and any scheduled maintenance.
- Vacation / swapping: use the on-call schedule tool (PagerDuty scheduling UI) and notify the on-call manager.

Game days and exercises:
- Frequency: bi-quarterly departmental game days and at least one company-wide game day per year.
- Goals: exercise runbooks, validate paging/comm flows, practice postmortems, and surface brittle automation.
- Typical scenarios: regional outage, model-serving overload, degraded KV cache, compromised credentials.
- Game day checklist: pre-announce, backup contacts, observation window, inject failure, run mitigation, debrief within 48 hours.

Postmortem process and template (blameless):
- Timeline: postmortem draft within 72 hours, review completed within 14 days, action items scheduled within 30 days.
- Template (use this as a checklist):
  - Title: Short, neutral description.
  - Incident ID and dates/times (UTC): detection -> mitigation -> resolution.
  - Severity and impact: customers affected, data loss (yes/no), downtime minutes.
  - Summary: 2-3 sentence overview.
  - Root cause analysis: evidence-backed causal chain.
  - Contributing factors: systemic and human.
  - Detection & mitigation timeline: bullet timeline of events and owners.
  - Corrective actions & owners: list of action items with owners and due dates.
  - Postmortem reviewer sign-offs and links to related tickets, dashboards, runbooks.

Status page & customer communications templates:
- Status page ownership: Product (content) + SRE (incidents & metrics) + Customer Success (customer-sensitive messaging).
- Status page cadence: update every 30 minutes for Sev1 and every 2 hours for Sev2 until resolution.

- Initial acknowledgement template (customer-facing):
  Subject: Redwood Inference — Incident acknowledged (ID: <INCIDENT_ID>)
  Body:
  Hello,
  We are currently investigating an issue affecting the Redwood Inference service impacting <summary of impact>. Our engineers are working to identify the cause and mitigate impact. We will provide an update within 30 minutes.
  Status: Investigating
  Impacted services: <list routes/models/regions>
  Start time (UTC): <timestamp>
  Incident ID: <INCIDENT_ID>
  For urgent account-specific concerns, contact your Customer Success manager.

- Update template (customer-facing):
  Subject: Redwood Inference — Incident update (ID: <INCIDENT_ID>)
  Body:
  Hello,
  Update: <summary of changes and impact>.
  Mitigation steps taken: <failover, rollback, scale>.
  Next update expected: <time or conditions>.
  Status: Identified / Mitigating / Monitoring

- Resolution template (customer-facing):
  Subject: Redwood Inference — Incident resolved (ID: <INCIDENT_ID>)
  Body:
  Hello,
  The incident affecting <services> has been resolved as of <timestamp> (UTC). Summary: <short summary of cause and fix>.
  Postmortem: A full postmortem will be published to customers/internal teams by <date>.
  If you experienced residual issues, please contact support.

Tools & integrations:
- PagerDuty: paging, on-call schedules, escalation policies.
- Slack: incident channels (#incident-<id>) with pinned runbook and status updates.
- Grafana & Prometheus: monitoring and alerting dashboards.
- Platform API: control plane calls for routing, failover, and rollbacks.
- Jira: incident tasks and postmortem tracking.
- Statuspage or internally-hosted status system: public status and incident history.

Metrics, reporting & continuous improvement:
- Incidents and MTTR tracked monthly and quarterly by severity and team.
- Postmortem action item completion rate tracked; target 90% of actions completed or re-triaged within 30 days.
- Runbook coverage target: 95% of top 20 on-call alert signatures should have an associated runbook.

Ownership & governance:
- On-call manager owns schedule hygiene, training, and postmortem governance.
- SRE director reviews Sev1 postmortems quarterly and reports systemic trends to executive leadership.

Appendices and quick references:
- Quick commands:
  kubectl get pods -n inference-fleet --selector app=inference-runtime
  kubectl logs -n inference-fleet <pod> --since=15m
  curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $RD_API_TOKEN' https://platform-api.redwood.internal/v1/health
- Contacts: PagerDuty lifecycle policy and escalation matrix are linked in the on-call handbook.
- Example links: Retail dashboards: grafana.redwood.internal/d/retail/inference-overview; Routing control plane docs: confluence/eng-platform/route-management.

Revision history:
- 2024-08-15: initial consolidated playbook (Ava Martinez).
- 2025-06-04: added game day schedule and updated runbook templates (SRE).
- 2026-01-12: updated severity definitions and on-call rotation cadence; clarified customer comms (Ava Martinez).

End of document.
